He played four seasons of [[college basketball]] for the [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence Friars]] before being drafted with the fifth overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]] by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]]. He played his rookie season with the Timberwolves before being traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in 2017. Dunn signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]] as a free agent in November 2020, but only played nine games for the team due to ankle surgery. ==High school career== Dunn attended [[New London High School (Connecticut)|New London High School]] in [[New London, Connecticut]]; he was one of the most dominating [[point guard]]s in high school basketball. During his junior year in 2010–11, Dunn averaged 26.5 points, 10 rebounds, 5 steals and 5 assists per game to lead the Whalers to a 27–0 record and a victory in the Connecticut Class L State Championship against Northwest Catholic High School. In his senior year from 2011 to 2012, he scored his 2,000th career point. He also led New London High School to the semifinal round of the 2012 Connecticut Class LL State Championships where they were defeated by St. Josephs High School.{{Cite news |title=CIAC Boys Basketball Tournament Schedule, Scores |url=http://articles.courant.com/2014-03-20/sports/hc-hs-boys-bb-tourney-agate-0306-20140305_1_fairfield-prep-hillhouse-basketball-tournament-schedule |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140428000417/http://articles.courant.com/2014-03-20/sports/hc-hs-boys-bb-tourney-agate-0306-20140305_1_fairfield-prep-hillhouse-basketball-tournament-schedule |archive-date=2014-04-28 |access-date=2025-10-27 |work=Hartford Courant |language=en}} Dunn was ranked #24 out of all high school players nationwide. He was also #1 in Connecticut. Dunn announced his intention to attend Providence College in August 2011.{{cite news |last=Morelli |first=Joe |date=August 24, 2011 |title=New London's Kris Dunn opts for Providence |work=MiddletownPress.com |url=http://www.middletownpress.com/articles/2011/08/24/sports/doc4e55995a5cdf1091384637.txt |url-status=dead |access-date=April 13, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120906004542/http://www.middletownpress.com/articles/2011/08/24/sports/doc4e55995a5cdf1091384637.txt |archive-date=September 6, 2012}} ==College career== Dunn tore his labrum in June 2012 and underwent shoulder surgery immediately. He made his freshman debut in late December.{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=December 6, 2012 |title=Providence's Kris Dunn expected to return before Christmas |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/providences-kris-dunn-expected-to-return-before-christmas |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=cbssports.com}} He played 25 games that season and averaged 5.7 points per game.[http://www.friars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kris_dunn_810465.html "Kris Dunn"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160629092510/http://www.friars.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/kris_dunn_810465.html |date=2016-06-29}}. friars.com. Retrieved February 26, 2016. On December 11, 2013, it was announced Dunn would undergo shoulder surgery and miss the rest of his sophomore season{{cite web |date=December 11, 2013 |title=Kris Dunn out for season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/10119067 |access-date=December 21, 2013 |publisher=ESPN.com news service}} after playing four games. In the 2014–15 season, Dunn returned from injury to earn the [[Big East]] Player of the Year and the Defensive Player of the Year awards. He averaged 15.6 points per game and led the Big East in assists per game and steals per game. Choosing to return for the 2015–16 season with the intention of graduating, Dunn garnered many preseason accolades, including preseason POY. Dunn was named Big East Player of the Week on January 4, 2016, after scoring 26 points in a win against [[2015–16 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]] and a 26-point outing in a victory over ninth-ranked [[2015–16 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]].{{cite web|title=Providence's Dunn, Villanova's Brunson Take MBB Weekly Honors|url=http://www.bigeast.com/news/2016/1/4/MBB_0104162903.aspx|website=[[Big East Conference]]|access-date=January 17, 2016|date=January 4, 2016}} On February 1, 2016, he was named one of 10 finalists for the Bob Cousy Point Guard of the Year Award.{{cite news|last=Nortlander|first=Matt|title=Cat Barber, Fred VanVleet missing from list of Cousy Award finalists|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25468790/cat-barber-fred-vanvleet-conspicuously-missing-from-cousy-award-finalists|access-date=February 2, 2016|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=February 1, 2016}} He was named to the 35-man midseason watchlist for the [[Naismith Trophy]] on February 11.{{cite news|last=Payne|first=Terrence|title=Naismith Trophy midseason list announced|url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/oklahoma-sooners-buddy-hield-lsu-tigers-ben-simmons-naismith-trophy-35-finalists-021116|access-date=February 19, 2016|work=[[Fox Sports]]|date=February 11, 2016}} At the conclusion of his redshirt junior season, Dunn announced his intention to skip his final season of eligibility and enter the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/providence-kris-dunn-nba-draft-declare-top-prospect-032216|title=Providence guard Kris Dunn will enter NBA Draft|first=Lindsey |website=newsobserver.com}} ==Professional career== ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2016–2017)=== On June 23, 2016, Dunn was selected by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] with the fifth overall pick in the [[2016 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2016 |title=Timberwolves Select Guard Kris Dunn with the Fifth Overall Pick in the 2016 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-select-guard-kris-dunn-fifth-overall-pick-2016-nba-draft |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On July 7, he signed his rookie-scale contract with the Timberwolves and joined the team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |date=July 7, 2016 |title=Timberwolves Sign Kris Dunn |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-kris-dunn |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} Dunn scored a team-high 27 points in his Summer League debut.{{Cite web |date=July 9, 2016 |title=Dunn Puts On A Show In Loss To Nuggets |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/dunn-shines-summer-league-loss-nuggets |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He managed just two Summer League games before sitting out the rest of the tournament after being diagnosed with a concussion.{{Cite web |date=July 12, 2016 |title=Tuesday's Wolves Links: How much is Karl-Anthony Towns worth? |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nba/post/_/id/22267 |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He made his regular season debut on October 26 in the Timberwolves' season opener, scoring eight points off the bench in a 102–98 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899386|title=Timberwolves vs. Grizzlies - Game Recap - October 26, 2016 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} On November 1, he had 10 points, six assists and five steals in his first career start, helping the Timberwolves defeat the Grizzlies 116–80.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899502|title=Grizzlies vs. Timberwolves - Game Recap - November 1, 2016 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com}} On December 6, he had a season-best game with 15 points on 6-for-7 shooting in a 105–91 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2016 |title=Spurs vs. Timberwolves - Game Recap - December 6, 2016 - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/400899761 |access-date=August 6, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} ===Chicago Bulls (2017–2020)=== On June 22, 2017, Dunn was traded, along with [[Zach LaVine]] and the rights to [[Lauri Markkanen]] (the 7th pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]]), to the [[Chicago Bulls]] in exchange for [[Jimmy Butler]] and the rights to [[Justin Patton]] (the 16th pick in the 2017 NBA draft).{{cite web |last=Dukich |first=Luka |date=June 22, 2017 |title=Bulls acquire Dunn, LaVine and Markkanen from Minnesota |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-acquire-dunn-lavine-and-markkanen-minnesota |access-date=August 6, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} His debut with the Bulls was delayed until the fifth game of the season after he suffered a left index finger dislocation during a preseason game on October 6. In his debut on October 28, in a 101–69 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Dunn came off the bench and had eight points and five fouls, while also aggravating his finger.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974830|title=Anthony scores 21 to lead Thunder's 101–69 rout of Bulls|work=ESPN.com|date=October 28, 2017|access-date=October 29, 2017}} On November 17, 2017, he scored a career-high 22 points in a 123–120 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974973|title=Holiday scores 27, Bulls hold off Walker, Hornets 123–120|work=ESPN.com|date=November 17, 2017|access-date=November 17, 2017}} On December 9, 2017, he had 17 points, nine assists and seven rebounds and made two free throws with 2.9 seconds left to lift the Bulls to a 104–102 victory over the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975131|title=Dunn hits late free throws, Bulls edge Knicks 104–102|work=ESPN.com|date=December 9, 2017|access-date=December 10, 2017}} On December 26, 2017, he recorded 20 points and 12 assists in 33 minutes in a 115–106 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975247|title=Mirotic scores 24 points off bench, Bulls beat Bucks 115–106|work=ESPN.com|date=December 26, 2017|access-date=December 26, 2017}} He also had four steals and two blocks against the Bucks; Dunn joined [[Michael Jordan]] as the only Bulls player with at least 20 points, 12 assists, four steals and two blocks in a game. He also became one of only 18 players to have amassed that stat line in an NBA game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975255|title=Bulls rally for a 92–87 win over Knicks|work=ESPN.com|date=December 27, 2017|access-date=December 28, 2017}} On January 5, 2018, he scored a career-high 32 points in a 127–124 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975318|title=Dunn gets career-high 32 as Bulls hold off Mavs 127–124|work=ESPN.com|date=January 5, 2018|access-date=January 6, 2018}} On February 14, 2018, he had eight points and three assists in 20 minutes against the [[Toronto Raptors]] after missing 11 games because of a concussion.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975605|title=Lowry leads Raptors to 7th win in row, 122–98 over Bulls|work=ESPN.com|date=February 14, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018}} Dunn missed the first two games of the 2018–19 season for the birth of his first child.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070725|title=Jordan gets another double-double as Mavs top Bulls 115–109|work=ESPN.com|date=October 22, 2018|access-date=December 10, 2018}} After recording nine points and seven assists on October 22 against the Dallas Mavericks, Dunn was sidelined with a sprained [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] in his left knee.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2018/10/23/bulls-kris-dunn-out-4-6-weeks-mcl-sprain|title=Bulls lose Kris Dunn for 4 to 6 weeks with MCL sprain|work=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2018|access-date=October 23, 2018}} On December 10, after sitting out nearly seven weeks, Dunn returned to the lineup and finished with nine points in 20 minutes in a 108–89 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071075|title=Fox sparks 2nd-half rally, Kings beat Bulls 108–89|work=ESPN.com|date=December 10, 2018|access-date=December 10, 2018}} On December 15, he scored 24 points in a 98–93 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071114|title=Dunn, Markkanen rally Bulls late to beat Spurs, 98–93|work=ESPN.com|date=December 15, 2018|access-date=December 16, 2018}} On January 4, he had 16 points and 17 assists in a 119–116 overtime loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071245|title=Victor Oladipo hits late 3, Pacers beat Bulls 119–116 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=January 4, 2019|access-date=January 5, 2019}} On March 20, he scored a season-high 26 points—including eight in overtime—to go with 13 assists in a 126–120 overtime win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071742|title=Markkanen, Dunn lead Bulls over Wizards 126–120 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=March 20, 2019|access-date=March 21, 2019}} In the [[2019–20 NBA season|2019–20 season]], Dunn finished eleventh in [[NBA All-Defensive Team|All-Defensive team]] voting. Although he narrowly missed out on both All-Defensive First and Second team, he received the only votes out of the players on a non playoff team or in the [[2020 NBA Bubble|experimental "bubble" in Orlando]]. Dunn received four first team votes and twenty-three second team votes. ===Atlanta Hawks (2020–2021)=== On November 28, 2020, Dunn signed a two-year, $9.7 million contract with the [[Atlanta
